plan.title: First Principles Thinking
plan.author: Mental model
plan.confidence_note: This is a mental model, not a book. The origin is attributed to Aristotle's definition of a first principle. The battery example and figures come from a widely reported 2012 Elon Musk interview, as given in the notes.
plan.one_liner: Stop copying how it's always done. Find what's certainly true, and build your answer from there.
plan.summary: First principles thinking means breaking a problem down to what you know is definitely true, then building your answer up from there. Usually we reason by analogy instead. We copy how things have always been done, or how others do them. That is quick, but it inherits other people's assumptions. The idea goes back to Aristotle, who described a first principle as the first basis from which a thing is known. Famously, in a 2012 interview, Elon Musk described battery packs costing around 600 dollars per kilowatt hour, yet the raw materials cost around 80. The real cost was in how packs were made. To use it, ask what you know for certain, and what you are only assuming.
